interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is documented. Positive surgical margins is documented. Seminal vesicle invasion is documented. Lymphovascular invasion is reported absent. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 38.59 months. This is a predicted recurrence horizon, not evidence of observed recurrence. The sensitivity range is 30.87–46.31 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. The preoperative PSA was elevated at 12. The surgical findings indicate a high-risk profile, specifically a Gleason 4+3 with tertiary pattern 5 (ISUP grade group 3), positive surgical margins, and invasion of the seminal vesicles. Conversely, there was no lymph node metastasis documented. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy difference is noted as the Gleason pattern and ISUP report are missing from the biopsy documentation. Missing nodal sampling is not an issue as nodes were sampled. The numeric horizon suggests a risk profile with a predicted recurrence horizon of 38.59 months. Information that would significantly revise this prognosis includes the postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory, as this directly informs the risk assessment. The current data suggests a relatively long horizon for recurrence.

attempts.text:
The patient underwent a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage of pT3b, positive surgical margins, and invasion of the seminal vesicles. The surgical pathology report documented "Gleason 4+3 with tertiary pattern 5 (ISUP grade group 3)," and "surgical margins were positive; the seminal vesicles were invaded; lymphovascular invasion was absent; there was no lymph node metastasis." The absence of lymph node metastasis is a favorable finding.

Preoperative factors include a PSA of 12. The positive margins and seminal vesicle invasion are concerning features. The nodal status is documented as no lymph node metastasis. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy difference is noted as the Gleason pattern and ISUP report are missing from the biopsy.

The prognosis is informed by these findings, with an expert horizon suggesting a 38.59-month horizon to recurrence. Information that would revise this prognosis significantly includes the postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up data widens the uncertainty regarding the trajectory.
